rows: Many monkeys and apes have three kinds of cone, as you do, but the owl monkey has a single kind and the bushbaby has one as well. Some New World monkeys vary between individuals. We show colour with a two-channel reading, which is the app's own choice.
A stumptail macaque resolves about 21 cycles per degree, close to a person's 30. Marmosets are set near 30 by cone counts. We blur the whole picture to about 21.
Owl monkeys and bushbabies are nocturnal. Owl monkeys have only a rudimentary fovea, and they lack colour vision, so their picture is grey with little sharp middle.
A Pan-like chimpanzee skull allows about 115 degrees of lateral field on one side. The app's whole-field figure of 180 degrees is a pick, not a measurement.
The size of the sharp middle, the dim-light gain, the whole-field figure and the blend of colour are the app's guesses. No record gave them for these animals.

claims.how: The stumptail macaque record converts 1.4 arc minutes to 21.4 cycles per degree, so the value equals that record's converted figure.

Records show three cone classes in many monkeys, one in owl monkeys and bushbabies, and variation in capuchins; the matrix is the app's two-channel reading, not built from these records, so it is graded i.
